issues: Whether 'severe and prolonged' disability can be established under the CPP where the coverage period ended before the application and contemporaneous medical records from the relevant period are unavailable

The standard of proof and the weight to be given to medical evidence in CPP disability determinations, including reports prepared in an advocacy context and records from a treating physician who began treatment after the coverage period ended
Whether the 'reasonably expected to qualify' prong of the CPP disability test is satisfied given the claimant's education, training and work history
The relevance of a claimant's past earnings to the CPP disability analysis
The effect of a late application on the availability of CPP disability benefits and the period for which benefits may be paid retroactively
Whether receipt of provincial disability benefits shortly after the onset of disability is relevant evidence in a CPP disability determination
key_facts: Claimant applied for CPP disability approximately sixteen years after his coverage period ended
Coverage period ended at the end of the year of a violent assault that caused PTSD
Contemporaneous medical records from the relevant period are unavailable (treating physician retired, records lost)
Only available records are from a new family physician who began treatment eight years after the coverage period ended, which the government says show no significant limitations
A psychiatrist's report was prepared for a lawyer approximately one year after the assault
A recent report from the same psychiatrist is also available
Claimant has been on provincial disability benefits since shortly after the assault and has not worked since
Claimant's work history consists of low-paying entry-level jobs with long gaps on EI and welfare
Claimant's education is a high school diploma from abroad plus one year of ESL
Claimant also has long-standing back pain from an earlier workplace injury and a history of major depression
search_terms: incapable of engaging in any employment
